The Software Tax
## You don't pay for software.You pay people to operate it.
The real cost was never the license. It's the labor stacked around it — the hours your own people spend keeping the software fed.
### License cost
The number on the invoice. It's the smallest part of what you actually pay, and the only part anyone talks about.
VISIBLE
### Admin cost
Someone has to configure it, maintain it, and keep the data clean. That someone is on your payroll.
HIDDEN
### Consultant cost
You pay outsiders to make your own systems work the way your business already works.
PAINFUL
90%
Your people's hours — the real expense
Every hour spent operating software is an hour not spent building. That's where the money really goes — often 90% of the true cost of ownership.
Meet Otto
## Understands the work, does the work, connects the company, and builds what you need.
![Otto at work](https://briq.ai/assets/deck-otto-tire-BRMV2BQq.jpg)
/01
### Conversation-first
You don't operate Otto — you talk to it. No screens to learn, no forms to fill, no training day. Say it once, plainly, and it's already moving.
/02
### Autonomous
Otto does the work — entry, follow-ups, reconciliations, reports. Give it a little and it runs. It doesn't suggest tasks; it completes them.
/03
### Orchestrated
Work flows end-to-end, sales to field to finance — nobody rekeying it into the next tool. One brain, one thread, no handoffs.
/04
### Generative
Otto builds the apps and workflows your business needs, on demand. No admins, no consultants, no roadmap to wait on.

03

Built from the ground up on construction workflows and financials. Otto already knows what a schedule of values is. It arrives fluent in your industry.

The Money
## Here's the money.
Value_01
### Licenses out
CRM seats to $0 at renewal. PM seats to $0 as projects roll off. ERP down to the 2 ledger seats accounting actually needs.
Value_02
### Hours back
Hours a week of data entry, rekeying, chasing, and reporting — returned per PM, per project accountant, per exec.
Value_03
### Cash faster
Billing out in days instead of weeks. Fewer missed change orders. Retention tracked, not forgotten.
Value_04
### Consultants gone
No more paying outsiders to configure your own systems. Otto generates what you need.
Line one alone usually pays for Briq. Lines two through four are the reason you'll wonder why you waited.
The Honest Slide
## Nobody rips out an ERP on a Tuesday.Here's how this actually goes.
The migration is deliberate, staged, and reversible at every step. But every stage has a date — and every date is a system you stop paying for.
The Replacement Schedule
## This is a replacement, not a coexistence.Every system gets a date.
CRMThe pipeline moves to Otto day one.
Salesforce gets a 60–90 day bridge, then a read-only archive — and $0 at renewal.
PMNew projects start on Otto.
In-flight jobs finish where they started. The last legacy closeout is your PM suite's termination date.
ERPModule retirement, one bite per quarter.
AP invoice processing, then billing and pay apps, then job cost, then compliance and lien waivers.
End state, on a date: Otto + a 2-seat ledger.
![Machine ready in the garage](https://briq.ai/assets/deck-f1-garage-DhF4swOs.jpg)
The First 90 Days
## What actually happens after you sign.
Phase 01
### Days 1–30
Otto connects and reads — email, plans, Salesforce, Procore, ERP. No behavior change asked of anyone yet. First autonomous workflow live by day 30.
Phase 02
### Days 31–60
New projects start on Otto. New opportunities born in Otto, pushed to Salesforce across the bridge. The first “wait, I didn't have to enter that anywhere?” moment happens in a meeting.
Phase 03
### Days 61–90
ROI review with your numbers — hours returned, invoices processed. The replacement schedule gets its final dates. Every date has a dollar figure on it.
